title: The Alerts Are Specific. The Capacity Gaps Are Already Here.
method: AI-assisted cross-source synthesis with direct links to originating publishers. Reviewed against a five-item gate supported by direct MSF and WHO primary publications.

items.headline: ADF-linked attacks kill at least 22 civilians across eastern Congo communities.
items.whyItMatters: The attacks join civilian protection, border security and outbreak control in the same operating terrain. The death and abduction counts remain provisional and were reported by local monitoring groups.

items.headline: South Sudan’s December election is advancing without settled confidence in the peace framework.
items.whyItMatters: The calendar is moving faster than the conditions needed for an inclusive and credible vote. Whether preparations, participation and post-election dialogue can be completed remains unresolved.

items.source: Médecins Sans Frontières / World Health Organization
items.headline: Primary responders say Congo’s Ebola resources are not reaching the frontline.
items.whyItMatters: The constraint is no longer only resource mobilisation; it is conversion of money, staffing and supplies into reliable field operations. MSF’s figures describe its operating areas and should not be generalized to every affected province.

items.headline: Ethiopian families reaching Kenya face registration and nutrition gaps.
items.whyItMatters: Safety at the border does not complete protection when registration, food and maternal or child health support lag behind arrivals. The 50,000 figure is a local-authority estimate, not a verified UNHCR count.

items.headline: Kenya moves from regional El Niño planning to local flood logistics.
items.whyItMatters: The measures give the regional warning an operating form: shelters, drainage work and communications. Preparedness cannot be inferred as sufficient until those plans are staffed, supplied and accessible to residents who cannot afford to move.
